entries.0536784a80909018: This category covers power and steam supply and transportation and warehousing operations, among others, and the company notes it as an operating segment not included in reportable segments. It includes Sumitomo Seika Chemicals Co., Ltd. and others. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥45,763 million (down 54.2% year on year), segment profit (core operating profit) was ¥4,394 million, and the number of employees was 1,305. The company cites as reasons for the decline in revenue and profit that the radiopharmaceutical diagnostics business and other businesses were sold and deconsolidated from the company in the previous consolidated fiscal year, and that the one-time gain from that sale no longer recurred.
entries.0d5bcd26b3e7b7b5: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells agricultural chemicals, fertilizers, agricultural materials, household and sanitary insecticides, materials for tropical infectious disease control, feed additives and other products. These are handled by Sumitomo Biorational Company LLC, Valent BioSciences LLC, Valent U.S.A. LLC, Sumitomo Chemical Brasil Industria Quimica S.A., Sumitomo Chemical Chile S.A., Sumitomo Chemical India Limited, among others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥519,256 million (down 3.9% year on year), and segment profit (core operating profit) was ¥56,334 million, the second-largest profit among the five reportable segments after Sumitomo Pharma. The number of employees was 7,016, and segment assets were ¥819,631 million, the largest of the six business segments. The company explains that while agricultural chemicals shipped firmly in Japan and overseas, shipments of the feed additive methionine declined. In addition to soybean use in South America, it began selling the fungicide Indiflin in India for paddy rice, and in Japan it launched the fungicide Fusekiwaido Flowable, which contains the new-mode-of-action active ingredient pyridachlometyl.

entries.2ac5e195cbf695b0: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells optical products, semiconductor process materials, compound semiconductor materials, touch sensor panels, high-purity aluminum and alumina, chemical products, additives, engineering plastics, battery components and other products. These are handled by Toyu Fine Chem Co., Ltd., Sumika Semiconductor Materials Texas, Inc., SSLM Co., Ltd., Sumika Electronic Materials Technology (Wuxi) Co., Ltd., Sumika Technology Co., Ltd., Tanaka Kagaku Kenkyusho Co., Ltd., and Taoka Chemical Co., Ltd., among others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥574,162 million (down 5.4% year on year), and segment profit (core operating profit) was ¥53,041 million. The number of employees, 9,563, was the largest of the six business segments, and capital expenditure of ¥52,970 million was also the largest. The company cites as reasons for the revenue decline the fall in selling prices of display-related materials, the impact of fundamental structural reform of the polarizing film business for large liquid crystal displays (LCDs), and lower export proceeds accompanying the stronger yen. On the other hand, it states that semiconductor process materials continued to recover gradually in market conditions and shipment volumes increased. In fiscal 2025, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemicals Corporation of Taiwan, gaining semiconductor chemicals bases in Taiwan and the United States.
entries.2ac7a91be7edd9ef: This is a reportable segment engaged in CDMO (process development and contract manufacturing) business in the advanced small-molecule pharmaceuticals, medical oligonucleotide and regenerative and cell medicine fields, among others. Koei Chemical Co., Ltd. and others take charge of it. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥58,601 million (down 5.7% year on year), segment profit (core operating profit) was ¥2,818 million, and the number of employees was 2,161. The company explains that while production of oligonucleotides ramped up in earnest and shipments increased, there were differences in product mix for active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates. In medical oligonucleotides, it strengthened its customer support structure by leveraging its U.S. base, and in regenerative and cell medicine, Amchepry®, the world's first iPS cell-derived product for Parkinson's disease treatment approved in Japan, received conditional and time-limited approval. The company positions its CDMO business as the core of its growth.

entries.4c6d2f835e0f76ce: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells synthetic resins, synthetic fiber raw materials, various industrial chemicals, methacrylates, synthetic resin processed products, ordinary alumina, synthetic rubber and other products. These are handled by Nihon Singapore Sekiyu Kagaku K.K., PCS (Private) Limited, The Polyolefin Company (Singapore) Private Limited, Rabigh Refining and Petrochemical Company (Petro Rabigh), among others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥678,800 million (down 24.5% year on year), the largest of the five reportable segments; segment profit (core operating profit) was ¥14,446 million, and the number of employees was 3,030. The company cites as reasons for the revenue decline the reduced shipments by sales subsidiaries associated with regular maintenance at Petro Rabigh, an equity-method affiliate; lower shipments of aluminum and other products due to the withdrawal from a business in the previous consolidated fiscal year; and lower shipments of synthetic resins due to a business transfer in the current consolidated fiscal year. As structural reform of the petrochemical business, from October 2025 it reduced its equity stake in Petro Rabigh to 15%, and in Japan it reached agreement with the parties concerned on optimizing operation of existing ethylene plants and integrating the polyolefin business.

entries.813b55babfd276d9: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells small-molecule pharmaceuticals. These are handled by Sumitomo Pharma Co., Ltd., Sumitomo Pharma America, Inc., Sumitomo Pharma Switzerland GmbH, Eurovant Sciences GmbH, among others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥451,933 million (up 13.6% year on year), and segment profit (core operating profit) was ¥108,444 million, the largest profit among the five reportable segments. The number of employees was 3,112. The company explains that revenue increased, owing to growth in North American sales of the prostate cancer treatment Orgovyx and the overactive bladder treatment Gemtesa, and to the recording of sales milestone income for Orgovyx. Core operating profit includes ¥50,024 million in profit related to the business transfer resulting from the sale of a portion of its interest in the Asia business. Sumitomo Pharma Co., Ltd. is a consolidated subsidiary, but its non-controlling interest ratio is 48.24%. There is no change in its status as a consolidated subsidiary even after the public offering of new shares in April 2026. In addition, the company notes that the revenue and core operating profit of this segment differ from those of Sumitomo Pharma Co., Ltd., a consolidated subsidiary, because, among other things, the CDMO business for regenerative and cell medicines does not belong to this segment.
